title.zh: 卷一百三十七 外國列傳一: 契丹
title.raw: 卷一百三十七 外國列傳一: 契丹 Volume 137: Foreign States Biographies 1 - Khitan

sentences.zh: 契丹者，古匈奴之種也。

translations.literal: The Khitan were the race of the ancient Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were descendants of the ancient Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 代居遼澤之中，潢水南岸，南距榆關一千一百里，榆關南距幽州七百里，本鮮卑之舊地也。

translations.literal: For generations they dwelt within the Liao marshes, on the south bank of the Huang River, one thousand one hundred li south of Yulin Pass; Yulin Pass lay seven hundred li south of Youzhou. This was the former territory of the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they lived in the Liao marshes on the south bank of the Huang River, eleven hundred li south of Yulin Pass—which in turn stood seven hundred li south of Youzhou—on what had once been Xianbei land.

sentences.zh: 其風土人物，世代君長，前史載之詳矣。

translations.literal: Their customs, land, and people, and the chieftains of each generation, have been recorded in detail in earlier histories.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs, territory, people, and successive chieftains are already treated at length in earlier histories.

sentences.zh: 唐咸通末，其王曰習爾之，疆土稍大，累來朝貢。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xiantong era of Tang, their king was called Xierzhi; his territory grew somewhat larger, and he repeatedly came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tang Xiantong period their king was Xierzhi; his domain expanded somewhat, and he sent tribute to court on repeated occasions.

sentences.zh: 光啟中，其王欽德者，乘中原多故，北邊無備，遂蠶食諸郡，達靼、奚、室韋之屬，咸被驅役，族帳浸盛，有時入寇。

translations.literal: In the Guangqi era, their king Qinde, taking advantage of the many troubles in the Central Plains and the lack of defenses on the northern frontier, then nibbled away at the various commanderies. The Tatars, Xi, Shiwei, and the like were all driven into service; tribal encampments grew ever more numerous, and at times they raided across the border.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangqi, King Qinde exploited turmoil in the Central Plains and the undefended northern frontier to encroach on neighboring prefectures. The Tatars, Xi, Shiwei, and kindred peoples were all pressed into service; Khitan camps multiplied, and they sometimes raided the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 劉仁恭鎮幽州，素知契丹軍情偽，選將練兵，乘秋深入，逾摘星嶺討之，霜降秋暮，即燔塞下野草以困之，馬多饑死，即以良馬賂仁恭，以市牧地。

translations.literal: Liu Rengong governed Youzhou and had long known the Khitan army's strengths and weaknesses. He selected generals and trained troops, and in autumn drove deep beyond Picking Star Ridge to attack them. When frost fell and autumn waned, he burned the grass below the passes to distress them; many horses starved to death. The Khitan then presented fine horses to bribe Rengong and purchase pasturelands.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong, military governor of Youzhou, knew the Khitan forces well. He picked commanders, drilled troops, and in autumn pushed deep beyond Picking Star Ridge to strike them. As frost came and autumn ended, he burned the grass along the frontier to starve their herds; many horses died. The Khitan then sent fine horses as gifts to buy grazing rights from Rengong.

sentences.zh: 仁恭季年荒恣，出居大安山，契丹背盟，數來寇鈔。

translations.literal: In his later years Rengong grew dissolute and wasteful, withdrew to dwell on Great Peace Mountain, the Khitan broke the alliance, and repeatedly came to raid and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years Rengong turned extravagant and withdrew to Great Peace Mountain. The Khitan broke their pact and raided the border again and again.

sentences.zh: 時劉守光戍平州，契丹實裏王子率萬騎攻之，守光偽與之和，張幄幕於城外以享之，部族就席，伏甲起，擒實裏王子入城。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Shouguang garrisoned Pingzhou. The Khitan prince Shili led ten thousand horsemen to attack him. Shouguang feigned peace, spread pavilions outside the walls to feast them, and when the tribesmen took their seats, hidden armored men rose up and seized Prince Shili into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouguang was then defending Pingzhou when the Khitan prince Shili attacked with ten thousand horsemen. Shouguang pretended to make peace, set up tents outside the walls for a banquet, and when the tribesmen sat down, armed men hidden in ambush seized Prince Shili and brought him into the city.

sentences.zh: 部族聚哭，請納馬五千以贖之，不許，欽德乞盟納賂以求之，自是十餘年不能犯塞。

translations.literal: The tribes gathered and wept, asking to offer five thousand horses as ransom; this was not granted. Qinde begged for alliance and offered bribes to obtain his release. From then on for more than ten years they could not violate the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes assembled in mourning and offered five thousand horses to ransom him, but Shouguang refused. Qinde sued for peace and paid lavish gifts to win the prince back. For more than a decade afterward the Khitan could not breach the frontier.

sentences.zh: 及欽德政衰，有別部長耶律阿保機，最推雄勁，族帳漸盛，遂代欽德為主。

translations.literal: When Qinde's rule declined, there was a chieftain of another branch, Yelu Abaoji, most esteemed for his valor; tribal encampments gradually flourished, and he thereupon replaced Qinde as chief.
translations.idiomatic: As Qinde's authority waned, Yelu Abaoji of another branch rose as the strongest leader; Khitan camps grew in power, and he supplanted Qinde as chief.

sentences.zh: 先是，契丹之先大賀氏有勝兵四萬，分為八部，每部皆號大人，內推一人為主，建旗鼓以尊之，每三年第其名以代之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Khitan forebears of the Dahe clan had forty thousand effective troops, divided into eight parts. Each part was styled a "great man," and within each they promoted one person as chief, raising banners and drums to honor him; every three years they ranked names and replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Dahe clan of the Khitan had forty thousand fighting men organized in eight tribes. Each tribe called its leader a "great man" and chose one man as chief, raising banners and drums in his honor; every three years they rotated the office by ranked succession.

sentences.zh: 及安巴堅為主，乃怙強恃勇，不受諸族之代，遂自稱國主。

translations.literal: When Abaoji became chief, he then relied on strength and trusted in courage, would not accept replacement by the various tribes, and thereupon styled himself lord of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Once Abaoji became chief, he leaned on his strength and refused the tribal rotation, proclaiming himself lord of the realm.

sentences.zh: 天祐四年，大寇雲中，後唐武皇遣使連和，因與之面會於雲中東城，大具享禮，延入帳中，約為兄弟，謂之曰：「唐室為賊所篡，吾欲今冬大舉，弟可以精騎二萬，同收汴、洛。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianyou he made a great raid on Yunzhong. The Martial Emperor of Later Tang sent envoys to join in alliance and met him face to face at the eastern citadel of Yunzhong, lavishly preparing a feast of honor and inviting him into the tent, pledging brotherhood. He said to him: "The house of Tang has been usurped by rebels. I intend a great campaign this winter; younger brother, you may bring twenty thousand picked horsemen and together recover Bian and Luo."
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou year 4 the Khitan raided Yunzhong on a large scale. Li Keyong, the Martial Emperor of Later Tang, sent envoys to ally with him and met him at the eastern citadel of Yunzhong, where he staged a grand banquet and received him in his tent as a sworn brother. Keyong said, "The Tang throne has been seized by rebels. I plan a major campaign this winter—you can bring twenty thousand elite horsemen, and together we shall retake Bian and Luoyang."

sentences.zh: 」安巴堅許之，賜與甚厚，留馬三千匹以答貺。

translations.literal: " Abaoji agreed; gifts bestowed were very generous, and he left three thousand horses in return for the presents.
translations.idiomatic: " Abaoji agreed. Keyong lavished gifts on him, and Abaoji left three thousand horses in return.

sentences.zh: 左右咸勸武皇可乘間擄之，武皇曰：「逆賊未殄，不可失信於部落，自亡之道也。

translations.literal: Those around him all urged the Martial Emperor to seize the chance and capture him. The Martial Emperor said: "The rebellious villains are not yet destroyed; one must not break faith with the tribes—that is the road to self-destruction."
translations.idiomatic: His advisers all urged Keyong to seize the moment and take Abaoji captive. Keyong replied, "The traitors are not yet destroyed. I cannot break faith with the tribes—that would be the path to ruin."

sentences.zh: 」乃盡禮遣之。

translations.literal: " He then sent him away with full courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: " He then dismissed him with full honors.

sentences.zh: 及梁祖建號，安巴堅亦遣使送名馬、女樂、貂皮等求封冊。

translations.literal: When the Founding Ancestor of Liang established his reign title, Abaoji also sent envoys presenting famous horses, female musicians, sable pelts, and the like, seeking investiture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Wen of Liang took the imperial title, Abaoji too sent envoys with fine horses, female musicians, sable furs, and other gifts seeking formal enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 梁祖與之書曰：「朕今天下皆平，唯有太原未服，卿能長驅精甲，徑至新莊，為我翦彼寇讎，與爾便行封冊。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor of Liang wrote to him: "I today have pacified all under Heaven; only Taiyuan is not yet subdued. If you can drive picked armor straight to Xinzhuang and cut down that enemy for me, I will at once carry out your enfeoffment."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen wrote to him: "I have now pacified the empire; only Taiyuan still holds out. If you can drive elite troops straight to Xinzhuang and destroy that foe for me, I will invest you immediately."

sentences.zh: 」莊宗初嗣世，亦遣使告哀，賂以金繒，求騎軍以救潞州，答其使曰：「我與先王為兄弟，兒即吾兒也，寧有父不助子耶！

translations.literal: " When Emperor Zhuangzong first succeeded to the throne, he also sent envoys to announce mourning, bribing with gold and silks and requesting cavalry to rescue Luzhou. He answered the envoy: "I and your former king were brothers; the son is my son—how could a father fail to aid his son!"
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Zhuangzong first took the throne, he too sent envoys to announce his father's death, offering gold and silks and asking for horsemen to relieve Luzhou. Abaoji told the envoy, "Your late king and I were brothers; his son is my son—would a father not help his child?"

sentences.zh: 」許出師，會潞平而止。

translations.literal: " He promised to send troops, but when Luzhou was pacified he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " He promised to march, but halted once Luzhou had fallen.

sentences.zh: 劉守光末年苛慘，軍士亡叛皆入契丹。

translations.literal: In his later years Liu Shouguang was harsh and cruel; soldiers who deserted and rebelled all entered the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In his final years Shouguang ruled with cruelty, and deserters from his ranks flocked to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 洎周德威攻圍幽州。

translations.literal: When Zhou Dewei attacked and besieged Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Dewei laid siege to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 燕之軍民多為所寇掠，既盡得燕中人士，教之文法，由是漸盛。

translations.literal: Many of Yan's soldiers and people were raided and plundered by them. Once they had obtained all the men of talent from Yan, they taught them written law, and from this gradually grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan raids ravaged the soldiers and people of Yan. Once they had gathered the educated elite of the region and taught them administration, their power steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 十三年八月，阿保機率諸部號稱百萬，自麟、勝陷振武，長驅雲、朔，北邊大擾。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the thirteenth year, Abaoji led the various tribes, claiming a force of a million, from Lin and Sheng to take Zhenwu, driving straight through Yun and Shuo; the northern frontier was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year 13, Abaoji led the tribes in a host said to number a million. Advancing from Lin and Sheng he seized Zhenwu and swept through Yun and Shuo, throwing the northern frontier into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 莊宗赴援於代，敵眾方退。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong went to aid from Dai, and only then did the enemy masses withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangzong marched to relieve them from Dai, and only then did the enemy withdraw.

sentences.zh: 十四年，新州大將盧文進為眾所迫，殺新州團練使李存矩於祁溝關，返攻新、武。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the great general of Xinzhou Lu Wenjin, pressed by the masses, killed the training commissioner of Xinzhou Li Cunju at Qigou Pass and turned back to attack Xin and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 Lu Wenjin, a senior general of Xinzhou, was driven by his troops to kill the training commissioner Li Cunju at Qigou Pass and rebel against Xin and Wu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 周德威以眾擊之，文進不利，乃奔於契丹，引其眾陷新州。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei struck him with troops; Wenjin fared poorly and then fled to the Khitan, leading his masses to seize Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei attacked him but Wenjin was beaten and fled to the Khitan, leading his men to capture Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 周德威率兵三萬以討之，北騎援新州，德威為敵所敗，殺傷殆盡，契丹乘勝攻幽州。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei led thirty thousand troops to punish him. Northern horsemen reinforced Xinzhou; Dewei was defeated by the enemy, killed and wounded nearly all, and the Khitan pressed the victory to attack Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei marched thirty thousand men against him, but Khitan horsemen reinforced Xinzhou, routed Dewei's army with near-total casualties, and pressed on to besiege Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時，或言契丹三十萬，或言五十萬，幽薊之北，所在北騎皆滿。

translations.literal: At that time some said the Khitan were three hundred thousand, others five hundred thousand; north of You and Ji, wherever one went northern horsemen filled the land.
translations.idiomatic: Reports then varied between three and five hundred thousand Khitan horsemen; north of You and Ji, the steppe seemed full of enemy cavalry wherever one looked.

sentences.zh: 莊宗遣明宗與李存審、閻寶將兵救幽州，遂解其圍，語在《莊宗紀》中。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong sent Emperor Mingzong together with Li Cunshen and Yan Bao to lead troops to rescue Youzhou, and thus lifted the siege; the account is in the "Annals of Emperor Zhuangzong."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong sent Mingzong, Li Cunshen, and Yan Bao to relieve Youzhou and break the siege; the fuller account appears in the Annals of Emperor Zhuangzong.

sentences.zh: 十八年十月，鎮州大將張文禮弒其帥王镕，莊宗討之，時定州王處直與文禮合謀，遣威塞軍使王郁復引契丹為援。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighteenth year, the great general of Zhenzhou Zhang Wenli murdered his commander Wang Yin; Emperor Zhuangzong campaigned against him. At that time Wang Chuzhi of Dingzhou conspired with Wenli and sent the commissioner of the Weisai Army Wang Yu to again lead the Khitan as reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 18 Zhang Wenli of Zhenzhou assassinated his lord Wang Yin, and Zhuangzong marched to punish him. Wang Chuzhi of Dingzhou joined the plot and sent Wang Yu of the Weisai Army to summon Khitan aid once more.

sentences.zh: 十二月，安巴堅傾塞入寇，攻圍幽州，李紹宏以兵城守。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Abaoji emptied the frontier passes in invasion, attacked and besieged Youzhou, and Li Shaohong defended the city with troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Abaoji poured the whole frontier into China, besieged Youzhou, and Li Shaohong held the walls.

sentences.zh: 契丹長驅陷涿郡，執刺史李嗣弼，進攻易、定，至新樂，渡沙河，王都遣使告急。

translations.literal: The Khitan drove straight forward and took Zhuo commandery, seized the prefect Li Sibi, advanced to attack Yi and Ding, reached Xinle, crossed the Sha River, and Wang Du sent envoys in urgent appeal.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan swept down, captured Zhuo, seized Prefect Li Sibi, pressed Yi and Ding, reached Xinle, crossed the Sha River, and Wang Du sent desperate appeals for help.

sentences.zh: 時莊宗在鎮州行營，聞前鋒報日「敵渡沙河」，軍中鹹恐，議者請權釋鎮州之圍以避之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Zhuangzong was in the field camp at Zhenzhou. Hearing the vanguard report day by day "the enemy has crossed the Sha River," the army was all afraid; advisers asked to provisionally lift the siege of Zhenzhou to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was then campaigning at Zhenzhou. Daily reports from the vanguard said the enemy had crossed the Sha River, and panic spread through the army. Some advisers urged him to raise the siege of Zhenzhou and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 莊宗曰：「霸王舉事，自有天道，契丹其如我何！

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong said: "When a hegemon-king undertakes affairs, Heaven has its own way—what can the Khitan do to me!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong said, "When a true conqueror acts, Heaven itself is on his side—what can the Khitan do to me?"

sentences.zh: 國初，突厥入寇，至於渭北，高祖欲棄長安，遷都樊、鄧，太守曰：「獫狁孔熾，自古有之，未聞遷移都邑。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state, the Turks invaded and reached north of the Wei. Gaozu wished to abandon Chang'an and move the capital to Fan and Deng. The prefect said: "The Xianyun are greatly rampant; they have existed since antiquity, but one has never heard of moving the capital."
translations.idiomatic: "At the dynasty's founding the Turks raided as far as the north bank of the Wei. Gaozu wanted to abandon Chang'an for Fan and Deng, but his minister said, 'Barbarian raids have always plagued China—no emperor ever saved himself by moving his capital.'"

sentences.zh: 霍去病，漢廷將帥，猶且誌滅匈奴，況帝王應運，而欲移都避寇哉！

translations.literal: Huo Qubing, a general of the Han court, still aspired to destroy the Xiongnu—how much more a Son of Heaven who receives the Mandate, yet wishes to move the capital to avoid raiders!"
translations.idiomatic: "Huo Qubing was only a Han general, yet he vowed to destroy the Xiongnu. How could an emperor who holds the Mandate think of fleeing his capital before barbarians?"

sentences.zh: 」文皇雄武，不數年俘二突厥為衛士。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wen was heroic and martial; within a few years he captured both Turks as palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Taizong was a warrior king; within a few years he had both Turkic khans captive as his bodyguards."

sentences.zh: 今吾以數萬之眾安集山東，王德明廝養小人，阿保機生長邊地，豈有退避之理，吾何面視蒼生哉！

translations.literal: Now I with tens of thousands of troops peacefully gather east of the mountains. Wang Deming is a menial groom's child; Abaoji grew up on the frontier—how could there be reason to retreat? How could I face the living masses!"
translations.idiomatic: "I hold east of the mountains with tens of thousands of men. Wang Deming is a stable boy's son, and Abaoji is a frontier chieftain—neither gives me cause to retreat. What face would I show the people if I ran?"

sentences.zh: 爾曹但駕馬同行，看吾破敵。

translations.literal: You lot need only mount your horses and come along—watch me break the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Mount up and ride with me—watch me smash the enemy."

sentences.zh: 」莊宗親禦鐵騎五千，至新城北，遇契丹前鋒萬騎，莊宗精甲自桑林突出，光明照日，諸部愕然緩退，莊宗分二廣以乘之，敵騎散退。

translations.literal: " Emperor Zhuangzong personally led five thousand iron cavalry to north of Xincheng, encountered ten thousand horsemen of the Khitan vanguard; Zhuangzong's picked armor burst forth from Mulberry Grove, light shining on the sun; the various tribes were startled and slowly withdrew; Zhuangzong divided two wings to press them, and the enemy horsemen scattered and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: " He led five thousand armored horsemen to the north of Xincheng and met ten thousand Khitan vanguard troops. His elite cavalry burst from Mulberry Grove in a blaze of sunlight; the tribes fell back in astonishment. Zhuangzong split his force in two wings and drove the enemy cavalry off in disorder."

sentences.zh: 時沙河微冰，其馬多陷，安巴堅退保望都。

translations.literal: At that time the Sha River had thin ice; many of their horses sank in; Abaoji withdrew to defend Wangdu.
translations.idiomatic: The Sha River was thinly frozen; many horses foundered, and Abaoji fell back to Wangdu.

sentences.zh: 是夜，莊宗次定州，翌日出戰，遇奚長托諾五千騎，莊宗親軍千騎與之鬥，為其所圍，外救不及，莊宗挺馬奮躍，出入數四，酣戰不解。

translations.literal: That night Emperor Zhuangzong halted at Dingzhou. The next day he went out to battle and met the Xi chieftain Tuonuo with five thousand horsemen. Zhuangzong's personal guard of a thousand horsemen fought them, was surrounded by them, and outside rescue could not reach in time. Zhuangzong spurred his horse and leaped fiercely, going in and out four or five times, fighting fiercely without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhuangzong camped at Dingzhou. The next day he met the Xi leader Tuonuo with five thousand horsemen. Zhuangzong's thousand-man guard clashed with them, was surrounded, and relief could not arrive in time. He spurred his horse and charged in and out of the encirclement four or five times, fighting on without respite.

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭聞其急也，灑泣而往，攻破敵陣，掖莊宗而歸。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao, hearing of his peril, went forth weeping, broke the enemy formation, and supported Emperor Zhuangzong back.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao, hearing of the danger, rushed forward in tears, broke the enemy line, and escorted Zhuangzong back to safety.

sentences.zh: 時契丹值大雪，野無所掠，馬無芻草，凍死者相望於路。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan encountered great snow; in the wilds there was nothing to plunder, horses had no fodder grass, and those who froze to death lined the road in sight of one another.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow fell on the Khitan; they could plunder nothing from the countryside, their horses had no fodder, and frozen corpses lined the roads.

sentences.zh: 安巴堅召盧文進，以手指天謂之曰：「天未令我到此。

translations.literal: Abaoji summoned Lu Wenjin, pointed with his finger to Heaven and said to him: "Heaven has not yet willed that I come here."
translations.idiomatic: Abaoji summoned Lu Wenjin, pointed to the sky, and said, "Heaven did not intend me to come this far."

sentences.zh: 」乃引眾北去。

translations.literal: " He then led the masses northward away.
translations.idiomatic: " He then led his army back north."

sentences.zh: 莊宗率精兵騎躡其後，每經安巴堅野宿之所，布稭在地，方而環之，雖去，無一莖亂者，莊宗謂左右曰：「蕃人法令如是，豈中國所及！

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong led picked troops and cavalry in pursuit behind them. Whenever he passed Abaoji's camps in the wild, straw was spread on the ground in squares and circled around; though they had departed, not a single stalk was disordered. Emperor Zhuangzong said to those at his side: "The laws and regulations of the barbarians are like this—how could China match them!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong pursued with elite cavalry. At every campsite Abaoji had used, straw was laid in neat squares and rings; even after the Khitan left, not a stalk was out of place. Zhuangzong told his attendants, "Barbarian discipline runs to this—China cannot equal it!"

sentences.zh: 」莊宗至幽州，發二百騎偵之，皆為契丹所獲，莊宗乃還。

translations.literal: " Emperor Zhuangzong reached Youzhou, sent out two hundred horsemen to scout them, and all were captured by the Khitan; Zhuangzong then returned.
translations.idiomatic: " At Youzhou he sent two hundred scouts; the Khitan captured them all, and Zhuangzong turned back."

sentences.zh: 天祐末，安巴堅乃自稱皇帝，署中國官號。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianyou, Abaoji thereupon styled himself emperor and appointed Chinese official titles.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tianyou era Abaoji proclaimed himself emperor and instituted Chinese-style offices.

sentences.zh: 其俗舊隨畜牧，素無邑屋，得燕人所教，乃為城郭宮室之制於漠北，距幽州三千里，名其邑曰西樓邑，屋門皆東向，如車帳之法。

translations.literal: Their custom had long followed pastoral herding; they had never had walled towns and houses. Taught by men of Yan, they then made the system of walled cities and palaces in the northern deserts, three thousand li from Youzhou, naming their settlement Western Tower City; house doors all faced east, like the method of cart tents.
translations.idiomatic: They had always lived as herders without permanent towns until men of Yan taught them to build cities and palaces on the northern steppe. Three thousand li from Youzhou they founded Western Tower City, with doors facing east as their tents had done.

sentences.zh: 城南別作一城，以實漢人，名曰漢城，城中有佛寺三，僧尼千人。

translations.literal: South of the city they separately built another city to settle Han people, called Han City; within the city were three Buddhist temples and a thousand monks and nuns.
translations.idiomatic: South of the capital they built a separate Han City for Chinese subjects, with three Buddhist temples and a thousand monks and nuns.

sentences.zh: 其國人號安巴堅為天皇王。

translations.literal: The people of their state called Abaoji the Heavenly Emperor King.
translations.idiomatic: His people called Abaoji the Heavenly Emperor King.

sentences.zh: 同光中，安巴堅深著辟地之志，欲收兵大舉，慮渤海踵其後。

translations.literal: In the Tongguang era, Abaoji deeply harbored ambitions to open territory; he wished to gather troops for a great campaign but feared Bohai would follow at his rear.
translations.idiomatic: During Tongguang, Abaoji was bent on expansion and planned a major campaign, but feared Bohai might strike from behind.

sentences.zh: 三年，舉其眾討渤海之遼東，令禿餒、盧文進據營、平等州，擾我燕薊。

translations.literal: In the third year he raised his masses to campaign against Liaodong of Bohai, ordered Tuyu and Lu Wenjin to hold Ying and Ping prefectures, and harassed our Yan and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he marched against Bohai's Liaodong, sent Tuyu and Lu Wenjin to seize Ying and Ping, and raided Yan and Ji.

sentences.zh: 明宗初纂嗣，遣供奉官姚坤奉書告哀，至西樓邑，屬阿保機在渤海，又徑至慎州，崎嶇萬里。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong first succeeded to the throne, he sent the palace attendant Yao Kun bearing a letter to announce mourning. Reaching Western Tower City, it happened that Abaoji was in Bohai; he again went straight to Shenzhou—a rugged ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong first took the throne he sent Yao Kun with a letter of condolence. Kun reached Western Tower City, learned Abaoji was campaigning in Bohai, and pressed on to Shenzhou—a journey of ten thousand rugged li.

sentences.zh: 既至，謁見阿保機，延入穹廬，阿保機身長九尺，被錦袍，大帶垂後，與妻對榻引見坤。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he had an audience with Abaoji, who invited him into the domed tent. Abaoji was nine chi in height, wore a brocade robe, a great belt hanging behind, and with his wife on facing couches introduced Kun.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Abaoji received him in his great tent. Nine chi tall, clad in brocade with a broad belt trailing behind, Abaoji and his wife received Kun from facing couches.

sentences.zh: 坤未致命，阿保機先問曰：「聞爾漢土河南、河北各有一天子，信乎？

translations.literal: Before Kun delivered his mission, Abaoji first asked: "I hear that in your Han lands south of the river and north of the river each has a Son of Heaven—is it true?"
translations.idiomatic: Before Kun could deliver his message, Abaoji asked, "I hear your Han lands now have one Son of Heaven south of the Yellow River and another north of it—is that so?"

sentences.zh: 」坤曰：「河南天子，今年四月一日洛陽軍變，今兇問至矣。

translations.literal: " Kun said: "The Son of Heaven south of the river—this year on the first day of the fourth month there was a military mutiny at Luoyang; now the dire news of his death has arrived."
translations.idiomatic: " Kun replied, "The southern emperor—on the first day of the fourth month this year there was a mutiny at Luoyang. News of his death has just arrived."

sentences.zh: 河北總管令公，比為魏州軍亂，先帝詔令除討，既聞內難，軍眾離心，及京城無主，上下堅冊令公，請主社稷，今已順人望登帝位矣。

translations.literal: The military governor north of the river, Lord Ling, recently because of the army turmoil at Weizhou, the late emperor issued an edict ordering his removal and punishment. Once he heard of internal troubles, the army and masses lost heart; when the capital had no master, above and below firmly enthroned Lord Ling, asking him to preside over the altars of soil and grain; he has now followed the people's hopes and ascended the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: "The northern commander, Lord Ling, had been sent to suppress a mutiny at Weizhou. When civil war broke out and the capital was left without a ruler, officers and men alike pressed him to take the throne. He has now ascended the imperial dignity in accord with popular expectation."

sentences.zh: 」阿保機號咷，聲淚俱發，曰：「我與河東先世約為兄弟，河南天子吾兒也。

translations.literal: " Abaoji wailed aloud, voice and tears both bursting forth, and said: "I and the former lord of Hedong pledged brotherhood; the Son of Heaven south of the river was my son."
translations.idiomatic: " Abaoji broke into loud wailing, voice and tears together, and said, "Your late king of Hedong and I were sworn brothers; the southern emperor was my son."

sentences.zh: 近聞漢地兵亂，點得甲馬五萬騎，比欲自往洛陽救助我兒，又緣渤海未下，我兒果致如此，冤哉！

translations.literal: Recently hearing of military turmoil in Han lands, I mustered fifty thousand armored horsemen and was about to go myself to Luoyang to rescue my son, but again because Bohai was not yet subdued, my son indeed came to this—how unjust!"
translations.idiomatic: "When I heard of turmoil in the Han lands I raised fifty thousand horsemen and was about to ride to Luoyang myself to save my son, but the Bohai campaign held me back—and now my son has come to this. How unjust!"

sentences.zh: 」泣下不能已。

translations.literal: " Tears fell and he could not stop.
translations.idiomatic: " He wept without cease.

sentences.zh: 又謂坤曰：「今漢土天子，初聞洛陽有難，不急救，致令及此。

translations.literal: He again said to Kun: "The present Son of Heaven of Han lands, when he first heard of trouble at Luoyang, did not urgently rescue him, causing matters to reach this point."
translations.idiomatic: He told Kun further, "Your new emperor, when he first heard of trouble at Luoyang, did not rush to help—and that is how things came to this pass."

sentences.zh: 」坤曰：「非不急切，地遠阻隔不及也。

translations.literal: " Kun said: "It was not that he was not urgent; the land was distant and barriers blocked him from reaching in time."
translations.idiomatic: " Kun said, "It was not lack of urgency—the distance was too great and the barriers too many to arrive in time."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「我兒既殂，當合取我商量，安得自便！

translations.literal: " He again said: "Now that my son has died, he ought to have consulted with me—how could he act on his own authority!"
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "Now that my son is dead, your emperor ought to have consulted me—how dare he act on his own!"

sentences.zh: 」坤曰：「吾皇將兵二十年，位至大總管，所部精兵三十萬，眾口一心，聖堅推戴，違之則立見禍生，非不知稟天皇王意旨，無奈人心何。

translations.literal: " Kun said: "Our emperor has commanded troops for twenty years, risen to great military governor; the picked troops under him number three hundred thousand, all mouths one heart. The sage firmly was pushed to ascend—to oppose would at once bring disaster. It is not that he did not know to report to the Heavenly Emperor King's intent; he was helpless before the people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: " Kun replied, "Our emperor has led armies for twenty years and commands three hundred thousand elite troops. Every voice was united in demanding his enthronement; to refuse would have brought immediate ruin. It is not that he ignored your wishes, Heavenly Emperor King—he could not defy the will of the army."

sentences.zh: 」其子托雲在側，謂坤曰：「漢使勿多談。

translations.literal: " His son Tuoyun was at his side and said to Kun: "Han envoy, do not talk overmuch."
translations.idiomatic: " His son Tuoyun, standing beside him, told Kun, "Han envoy, say no more."

sentences.zh: 」因引左氏牽牛蹊田之說以折坤，坤曰：「應天順人，不同匹夫之義，只如天皇王初領國事，豈是強取之耶！

translations.literal: " He thereupon cited from the Zuo Commentary the story of the Oxherd Star trampling fields to refute Kun. Kun said: "Responding to Heaven and following the people is not the same as the righteousness of a common man—just as when the Heavenly Emperor King first took charge of state affairs, was it by forcible seizure!"
translations.idiomatic: " He cited the Zuo Commentary tale of the Herd-Boy trampling another's fields to rebuke Kun. Kun answered, "Heaven's mandate and the people's will are not the petty morality of private quarrels—when you, Heavenly Emperor King, first took power, was that by force alone?"

sentences.zh: 」阿保機因曰：「理當如此，我漢國兒子致有此難，我知之矣。

translations.literal: " Abaoji then said: "It is right that it should be so. That my Han-state son brought on this difficulty—I already knew it."
translations.idiomatic: " Abaoji said, "That is only reasonable. I already knew my Han son would come to such grief."

sentences.zh: 聞此兒有宮婢二千，樂官千人，終日放鷹走狗，耽酒嗜色，不惜人民，任使不肖，致得天下皆怒。

translations.literal: I heard this son had two thousand palace maidservants and a thousand music officers, all day letting hawks fly and dogs run, addicted to wine and fond of women, not cherishing the people, employing unworthy men, causing all under Heaven to be angry.
translations.idiomatic: I heard he kept two thousand palace women and a thousand musicians, spent his days hawking and hunting, drowned himself in wine and women, wasted the people's strength, and put worthless men in office until the whole realm turned against him.

sentences.zh: 我自聞如斯，常憂傾覆，一月前已有人來報，知我兒有事，我便舉家斷酒，解放鷹犬，休罷樂官。

translations.literal: When I myself heard it was so, I constantly feared overthrow. A month ago someone had already come to report, knowing my son had trouble; I then had the whole household cut off wine, release hawks and dogs, and dismiss the music officers.
translations.idiomatic: When I heard such things I feared disaster for him. A month ago messengers told me he was in trouble, and my whole household gave up wine, released our hawks and dogs, and dismissed our musicians.

sentences.zh: 我亦有諸部家樂千人，非公宴未嘗妄舉。

translations.literal: I too have a thousand household musicians among the tribes, and except at public banquets I have never lightly raised them.
translations.idiomatic: I too keep a thousand tribal musicians, but never call them forth except at state banquets.

sentences.zh: 我若所為似我兒，亦應不能持久矣，從此願以為戒。

translations.literal: If what I did were like my son, I too should not be able to endure long; from this I wish to take it as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: If I acted as he did, I too could not last—and from this I take my warning.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「漢國兒與我雖父子，亦曾彼此讎敵，俱有惡心，與爾今天子無惡，足得歡好。

translations.literal: " He again said: "The Han-state son and I, though father and son, were also once mutual enemies; both harbored ill will. With your present Son of Heaven there is no ill will—sufficient to have friendly relations."
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "That Han son and I were father and son, yet we were also enemies and bore malice toward each other. With your present emperor there is no such ill will—we can be friends."

sentences.zh: 爾先復命，我續將馬萬騎至幽、鎮以南，與爾家天子面為盟約，我要幽州，令漢兒把捉，更不復侵入漢界。

translations.literal: You first return to report; I will continue with ten thousand horsemen south of You and Zhen to make a face-to-face covenant with your house's Son of Heaven. I want Youzhou—let Han men hold it—and I will no longer invade Han territory.
translations.idiomatic: Return first with your report. I will follow with ten thousand horsemen south of You and Zhen to seal a pact with your emperor in person. I want Youzhou held by Han men, and I will not again cross into Han territory.

sentences.zh: 」又問：「漢收得西川，信不？

translations.literal: " He again asked: "Did Han recover Western Chuan—is it true?"
translations.idiomatic: " He asked further, "Is it true that Han has taken Western Shu?"

sentences.zh: 」坤曰：「去年九月出兵，十一月十六日收下東、西川，得兵馬二十萬，金帛無算。

translations.literal: " Kun said: "Last year in the ninth month troops were sent out; on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month Eastern and Western Chuan were taken, obtaining two hundred thousand troops and horses, gold and silks beyond counting."
translations.idiomatic: " Kun said, "Troops marched last ninth month, and on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month both eastern and western Shu were taken—two hundred thousand soldiers and horses, and gold and silks beyond reckoning."

sentences.zh: 皇帝初即位，未辦送來，續當遣使至矣。

translations.literal: The emperor has just ascended the throne and has not yet been able to send them; envoys will be dispatched in due course.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor has only just taken the throne and has not yet been able to send gifts, but envoys will follow shortly.

sentences.zh: 」阿保機忻然曰：「聞西有劍閣，兵馬從何過得？

translations.literal: " Abaoji said with pleasure: "I hear to the west there is Sword Pass—how could troops and horses get through?"
translations.idiomatic: " Abaoji said delightedly, "I have heard of Sword Pass in the west—how could an army pass through it?"

sentences.zh: 」坤曰：「川路雖險，然先朝收復河南，有精兵四十萬，良馬十萬騎，但通人行處，便能去得，視劍閣如平地耳。

translations.literal: " Kun said: "Though Sichuan routes are perilous, yet the former dynasty recovered Henan with four hundred thousand picked troops and one hundred thousand fine horses. Wherever men can pass, one can go; Sword Pass is regarded as level ground."
translations.idiomatic: " Kun said, "The roads of Shu are steep, but when the former dynasty recovered Henan it had four hundred thousand elite troops and one hundred thousand fine horses. Wherever men can walk, troops can pass—Sword Pass is no more than level ground to us."

sentences.zh: 」阿保機善漢語，謂坤曰：「吾解漢語，歷口不敢言，懼部人效我，令兵士怯弱故也。

translations.literal: " Abaoji was skilled in Han speech and said to Kun: "I understand Han speech but through all my years have not dared speak it, fearing the tribesmen would imitate me and cause the soldiers to grow timid."
translations.idiomatic: " Abaoji knew Chinese and told Kun, "I understand your language but have never dared speak it openly, lest my tribesmen learn it and my warriors grow soft."

sentences.zh: 」坤至止三日，阿保機病傷寒。

translations.literal: " Kun had been there only three days when Abaoji fell ill with cold damage.
translations.idiomatic: " Kun had been there only three days when Abaoji fell ill with a cold fever.

sentences.zh: 一夕，大星殞於其帳前，俄而卒於扶餘城，時天成元年七月二十七日也。

translations.literal: One evening a great star fell before his tent; shortly he died at Fuyu City—on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month of the first year of Tiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: One night a great star fell before his tent, and soon afterward he died at Fuyu City, on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month of Tiancheng year 1.

sentences.zh: 其妻舒嚕氏自率眾護其喪歸西樓，坤亦從行，得報而還。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Shulü herself led the masses to escort the coffin back to Western Tower; Kun also followed on the journey, obtained the report, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Shulü led the tribes escorting the coffin back to Western Tower. Kun accompanied them, received his report, and returned.

sentences.zh: 既而舒嚕氏立其次子德光為渠帥，以總國事，尋遣使告哀，明宗為之輟朝。

translations.literal: Shortly Lady Shulü enthroned her second son Deguang as tribal chief to oversee state affairs; soon she sent envoys to announce mourning, and Emperor Mingzong suspended court for it.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shulü then installed her second son Deguang as chief to govern the realm and soon sent envoys announcing the death. Mingzong suspended court in mourning.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，葬阿保機於木葉山，偽謚曰「大聖皇帝」。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year Abaoji was buried on Mount Muye; his false posthumous title was "Great Sage Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: The following first month Abaoji was buried on Mount Muye with the posthumous title "Great Sage Emperor."

sentences.zh: 阿保機凡三子，皆雄偉。

translations.literal: Abaoji had three sons in all, all imposing in stature.
translations.idiomatic: Abaoji had three sons, all imposing men.

sentences.zh: 長曰人皇王突然，即東丹王也；

translations.literal: The eldest was called Human Emperor King Turyu—that is, the King of Eastern Dan;
translations.idiomatic: The eldest was Turyu, the Human Emperor King, ruler of Eastern Dan;

sentences.zh: 次曰元帥太子，即德光也；

translations.literal: the second was called Marshal Crown Prince—that is, Deguang;
translations.idiomatic: the second was the Marshal Crown Prince, Deguang;

sentences.zh: 幼曰阿安端君。

translations.literal: the youngest was called Lord A'anduan.
translations.idiomatic: the youngest was Lord A'anduan.

sentences.zh: 德光本名耀屈之，後慕中華文字，遂改焉。

translations.literal: Deguang's original name was Yaoquzhi; later, admiring the written characters of the Central States, he changed it accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang had been named Yaoquzhi, but later, enamored of Chinese writing, he adopted the new name.

sentences.zh: 唐天成初，阿保機死，其母令德光權主牙帳，令少子安端少君往渤海國代突欲。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Later Tang's Tiancheng, Abaoji died; his mother ordered Deguang provisionally to preside over the yak-tail tent, and ordered the younger son Young Lord A'anduan to go to the Bohai state to replace Tuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng, after Abaoji's death, his mother placed Deguang in provisional charge of the royal tent and sent the youngest son A'anduan to Bohai to replace Tuyu.

sentences.zh: 突欲將立，而德光素為部族所服，又其母亦常鐘愛，故因而立之。

translations.literal: Tuyu was about to be enthroned, but Deguang had long been obeyed by the tribes, and his mother also constantly favored him; therefore he was enthroned accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyu had been the expected heir, but the tribes had long respected Deguang and his mother favored him, so he was enthroned instead.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，德光遣使摩琳等三十餘人來修好，又遣使為父求碑石，明宗許之，賜與甚厚，並賜其母瓔珞錦彩。

translations.literal: In Emperor Mingzong's time, Deguang sent envoys Molin and more than thirty others to renew friendly relations, and also sent envoys to request a stele for his father. Mingzong granted it, bestowed gifts very generously, and also bestowed on his mother necklaces of gems and brocades.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong, Deguang sent Molin and more than thirty envoys to renew relations and asked for a memorial stele for his father. Mingzong agreed, lavished gifts on the embassy, and sent necklaces and brocades to Deguang's mother.

sentences.zh: 自是山北安靜，蕃漢不相侵擾。

translations.literal: From then on north of the mountains was peaceful; barbarians and Han did not mutually harass.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the country north of the mountains was at peace, and Khitan and Han did not raid one another.

sentences.zh: 三年，德光偽改為天顯元年。

translations.literal: In the third year Deguang falsely changed the era to the first year of Tianxian.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Deguang proclaimed the Tianxian era.

sentences.zh: 是歲，定州王都作亂，求援於契丹，德光陷平州，遣禿餒以騎五千援都於中山，招討使王晏球破之於曲陽，托諾走保賊城。

translations.literal: That year Wang Du of Dingzhou rebelled and sought aid from the Khitan. Deguang took Pingzhou and sent Tuyu with five thousand horsemen to aid Du at Zhongshan. The pacification commissioner Wang Yanqiu defeated them at Quyang; Tuonuo fled to hold the rebel city.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wang Du of Dingzhou rebelled and called on the Khitan. Deguang seized Pingzhou and sent Tuyu with five thousand horsemen to aid Du at Zhongshan. Wang Yanqiu, the pacification commissioner, routed them at Quyang, and Tuonuo fled into the rebel stronghold.

sentences.zh: 其年七月，又遣惕隱率七千騎救定州，王晏球逆戰於唐河北，大破之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year he again sent a tiyin leading seven thousand horsemen to rescue Dingzhou. Wang Yanqiu met them in battle on the north bank of the Tang River and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he sent a tiyin with seven thousand horsemen to relieve Dingzhou. Wang Yanqiu met them on the north bank of the Tang River and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 幽州趙德鈞以生兵接於要路，生擒惕隱等首領五十餘人獻闕下。

translations.literal: Zhao Dejun of Youzhou with fresh troops blocked the vital route and captured alive more than fifty leaders including the tiyin, presenting them at the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dejun of Youzhou blocked the key road with fresh troops, captured more than fifty Khitan leaders including the tiyin alive, and presented them at court.

sentences.zh: 明年，王都平，擒托諾及餘眾，斬之。

translations.literal: The next year Wang Du was pacified; Tuonuo and the remaining masses were captured and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wang Du's rebellion was crushed; Tuonuo and his remaining followers were captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 自是契丹大挫，數年不敢窺邊。

translations.literal: From then on the Khitan suffered a great setback and for several years did not dare peer at the border.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Khitan were badly defeated and for years did not dare probe the frontier.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣使挎括梅裏來求禿餒骸骨，明宗怒其詐，斬之。

translations.literal: They once sent the envoy Kuakuo Meili to request Tuyu's remains; Mingzong was angry at the deception and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: They once sent the envoy Kuakuo Meili to demand Tuyu's remains. Mingzong, angered by the ruse, had him executed.

sentences.zh: 長興二年，東丹王突欲在闕下，其母繼發使申報，朝廷亦優容之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changxing, Eastern Dan King Tuyu was at the imperial court; his mother continued to send envoys to report, and the court also treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing year 2 the Eastern Dan king Tuyu was at court; his mother kept sending envoys with reports, and the dynasty treated him leniently.

sentences.zh: 長興末，契丹迫雲州，明宗命晉高祖為河東節度使兼北面蕃漢總管。

translations.literal: At the end of Changxing the Khitan pressed Yunzhou; Mingzong appointed the Jin Founding Emperor military governor of Hedong and concurrently overall commander of barbarian and Han forces on the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Changxing the Khitan pressed Yunzhou, and Mingzong appointed the future Jin Founding Emperor military governor of Hedong and commander of all northern frontier forces, Han and barbarian alike.

sentences.zh: 清泰三年，晉高祖為張敬達等攻圍甚急，遣指揮使何福賫表乞師，願為臣子。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingtai the Jin Founding Emperor was pressed very hard in siege by Zhang Jingda and others; he sent the commander He Fubi with a memorial begging for troops and willing to become a subject.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingtai year 3 the Jin emperor was besieged by Zhang Jingda and others. He sent Commander He Fubi with a petition begging for troops and offering to become a vassal.

sentences.zh: 德光白其母曰：「兒昨夢太原石郎發使到國，今果至矣，事符天意，必須赴之。

translations.literal: Deguang told his mother: "Yesterday I dreamed that Stone Lord of Taiyuan sent an envoy to our state; now he has indeed arrived—the matter accords with Heaven's intent; I must go to aid him."
translations.idiomatic: Deguang told his mother, "Last night I dreamed that Lord Stone of Taiyuan had sent an envoy to us—and now he has come. Heaven wills this; I must go."

sentences.zh: 」德光乃自率五萬騎由雁門至晉陽，即日大破敬達之眾於城下，尋冊晉高祖為大晉皇帝，約為父子之國，割幽州管內及新、武、雲、應、朔州之地以賂之，仍每歲許輸帛三十萬。

translations.literal: " Deguang then personally led fifty thousand horsemen through Yanmen to Jinyang and the same day greatly defeated Jingda's masses below the walls. Shortly he enfeoffed the Jin Founding Emperor as Great Jin Emperor, pledged a father-and-son state, ceded the territory within Youzhou's jurisdiction and Xin, Wu, Yun, Ying, and Shuo prefectures as bribes, and still each year permitted delivery of three hundred thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: " He led fifty thousand horsemen through Yanmen Pass to Jinyang and the same day routed Zhang Jingda's army beneath the walls. He then enthroned the Jin emperor, pledged a father-and-son relationship between their states, ceded Youzhou and the prefectures of Xin, Wu, Yun, Ying, and Shuo as payment, and exacted an annual tribute of three hundred thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 時幽州趙德鈞屯兵於團柏谷，遣使至幕帳，求立己為帝，以石氏世襲太原，德光對使指帳前一石曰：「我已許石郎為父子之盟，石爛可改矣。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Dejun of Youzhou encamped troops at Tuanbai Valley, sent an envoy to the command tent, and asked to be enthroned himself while the Shi clan would hereditarily hold Taiyuan. Deguang answered the envoy, pointing at a stone before the tent: "I have already pledged brotherhood with Lord Stone—a stone may rot, but that cannot be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dejun of Youzhou was then encamped at Tuanbai Valley and sent an envoy offering to make himself emperor if the Shi clan could keep Taiyuan in perpetuity. Deguang pointed to a stone before his tent and told the envoy, "I have already sworn brotherhood with Lord Stone—a stone may crumble, but that oath cannot."

sentences.zh: 」楊光遠等殺張敬達降於契丹，德光戲謂光遠等曰：「爾輩大是惡漢兒，不用鹽酪，食卻一萬匹戰馬。

translations.literal: " Yang Guangyuan and others killed Zhang Jingda and surrendered to the Khitan. Deguang jested to Guangyuan and others: "You lot are truly wicked Han fellows—without salt or curds you devoured ten thousand war horses."
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Guangyuan and others killed Zhang Jingda and surrendered to the Khitan. Deguang joked to them, "You wretched Han—living without salt or dairy, yet you ate up ten thousand war horses."

sentences.zh: 」光遠等大慚。

translations.literal: " Guangyuan and the others were greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: " Guangyuan and his fellows were deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖南行，德光自送至潞州。

translations.literal: The Jin Founding Emperor went south; Deguang personally escorted him to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor marched south, and Deguang escorted him as far as Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 時趙德鈞、趙延壽自潞州出降於契丹，德光鎖之，令隨牙帳。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Dejun and Zhao Yanshou came out from Luzhou to surrender to the Khitan; Deguang put them in fetters and ordered them to follow the yak-tail tent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dejun and Zhao Yanshou then surrendered at Luzhou. Deguang put them in chains and kept them with his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖入洛，尋遣宰相趙瑩致謝於契丹。

translations.literal: The Jin Founding Emperor entered Luoyang and soon sent the chief minister Zhao Ying to express thanks to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Jin emperor entered Luoyang, he sent Chief Minister Zhao Ying to thank the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 天福三年，又遣宰臣馮道、左僕射劉句等持節冊德光及其母氏徽號，賫鹵簿、儀伏、法服、車輅於本國行禮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianfu he again sent the chief minister Feng Dao, Left Vice Director Liu Gou, and others bearing credentials to enfeoff Deguang and his mother's clan with honorific titles, carrying imperial regalia, ceremonial guards, court robes, and chariots to perform the rites in their state.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu year 3 he sent Feng Dao, Liu Gou, and others with credentials to invest Deguang and his mother with honorific titles, bearing imperial regalia, ceremonial guards, court robes, and chariots to perform the rites in the Khitan realm.

sentences.zh: 德光大悅，尋遣使奉晉高祖為英武明義皇帝。

translations.literal: Deguang was greatly pleased and soon sent envoys to honor the Jin Founding Emperor as Heroic Martial Illustrious Righteous Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang was delighted and in turn sent envoys to honor the Jin emperor as Heroic Martial Illustrious Righteous Emperor.

sentences.zh: 是歲，契丹改天顯十一年為會同元年，以趙延壽為樞密使，升幽州為南京，以趙思溫為南京留守，既而德光請晉高祖不稱臣，不上表，來往緘題止用家人禮，但云「兒皇帝」，晉祖厚賫金帛以謝之。

translations.literal: That year the Khitan changed the eleventh year of Tianxian to the first year of Huitong, appointed Zhao Yanshou as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, elevated Youzhou to Southern Capital, and appointed Zhao Siwen as Southern Capital military governor. Shortly Deguang requested that the Jin Founding Emperor not style himself subject or submit memorials; in correspondence they used only family rites, merely calling him "Son Emperor," and the Jin ancestor richly sent gold and silks in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Khitan renamed their eleventh Tianxian year as Huitong year 1, made Zhao Yanshou commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, elevated Youzhou to Southern Capital with Zhao Siwen as its governor, and persuaded the Jin court to drop the language of vassalage. Their correspondence used only familial terms, addressing the Jin ruler as "Son Emperor," for which the Jin emperor sent lavish gifts in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 晉祖奉契丹甚至，歲時問遺，慶吊之禮，必令優厚。

translations.literal: The Jin ancestor served the Khitan to the utmost; seasonal greetings and gifts, rites of congratulation and condolence—he always ordered them generous.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor courted the Khitan with extreme deference, ensuring that seasonal gifts and congratulatory or condolence missions were always lavish.

sentences.zh: 每北使至，即於別殿致敬。

translations.literal: Whenever northern envoys arrived, he at once paid respects in a separate hall.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Khitan envoys arrived, he received them with obeisance in a separate hall.

sentences.zh: 德光每有邀請，小不如意，則來譴責，晉祖每屈己以奉之，終晉祖世，略無釁隙。

translations.literal: Whenever Deguang had a request and was slightly displeased, he would come to rebuke; the Jin ancestor each time humbled himself to serve him. Through the Jin ancestor's reign there was scarcely any breach.
translations.idiomatic: If any request went slightly awry, Deguang would send reproaches, and the Jin emperor always humbled himself to comply. Through his reign there was scarcely a breach between them.

sentences.zh: 及少帝嗣位，遣使入契丹，德光以少帝不先承稟，擅即尊位，所賫文字，略去臣禮，大怒，形於責讓，朝廷使去，即加譴辱。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded to the throne, he sent envoys into the Khitan. Deguang, because the Young Emperor had not first reported and receive approval but on his own seized the exalted position, and the written documents he brought largely omitted the rites of subjecthood, was greatly angry, showing it in rebuke and blame. When the court's envoys departed, he at once added insult.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he sent envoys to the Khitan. Deguang was furious that the new ruler had taken the throne without prior approval and that his letters omitted the language of vassalage. He rebuked the envoys openly and insulted them on their departure.

sentences.zh: 會契丹回圖使喬榮北歸，侍衛親軍都指揮使景延廣謂榮曰：「先朝是契丹所立，嗣君乃中國自冊，稱孫可矣，稱臣未可。

translations.literal: It happened that the Khitan returning-map envoy Qiao Rong was going north. The commander of the Palace Guard Jing Yanguang said to Rong: "The former dynasty was established by the Khitan; the succeeding ruler was enthroned by China itself—calling him grandson is acceptable, calling him subject is not."
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan envoy Qiao Rong was returning north, Palace Guard Commander Jing Yanguang told him, "Your court made our former emperor; our present ruler was enthroned by China itself. He may call himself your grandson, but not your subject."

sentences.zh: 中國自有十萬口橫磨劍，要戰即來！

translations.literal: China itself has a hundred thousand mouths of swords for horizontal grinding—if you want battle, come!"
translations.idiomatic: China has a hundred thousand swords ready to grind on the whetstone—if you want war, come!"

sentences.zh: 」榮至本國，具言其事，德光大怒，會青州楊光遠叛，遣使構之。

translations.literal: " When Rong reached his state he reported the matter in full; Deguang was greatly angry. It happened that Yang Guangyuan of Qingzhou rebelled, and he sent envoys to incite him.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong reported this fully at home, and Deguang flew into a rage. When Yang Guangyuan rebelled at Qingzhou, Deguang sent envoys to encourage him.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，德光率諸部南下，開運元年春，陷祁州，直抵大河，少帝幸澶州以禦之。

translations.literal: The next winter Deguang led the various tribes south. In the spring of the first year of Kaiyun he took Qizhou, drove straight to the Great River, and the Young Emperor went to Chanzhou to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter Deguang marched south with the tribes. In the spring of Kaiyun year 1 he seized Qizhou, reached the Yellow River, and the Young Emperor went to Chanzhou to face him.

sentences.zh: 其年三月，德光敗於陽城，棄其車帳，乘一橐駝奔至幽州。

translations.literal: In the third month of that year Deguang was defeated at Yangcheng, abandoned his carts and tents, mounted a single camel, and fled to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was defeated at Yangcheng, abandoned his baggage train, fled on a single camel to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 因怒其失律，自大首領已下各杖數百，唯趙延壽免焉。

translations.literal: Angry at their breach of discipline, from the great chiefs downward each was flogged several hundred strokes; only Zhao Yanshou was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Furious at the defeat, he had every chief from the highest rank down flogged hundreds of strokes—only Zhao Yanshou was spared.

sentences.zh: 是時，契丹連歲入寇，晉氏疲於奔命，邊民被苦，幾無寧日，晉相桑維翰勸少帝求和於契丹，以紓國難，少帝許之，乃遣使奉表稱臣，卑辭首過。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan for successive years invaded; the Jin house was exhausted from rushing to respond; border people suffered hardship and scarcely had a peaceful day. The Jin chancellor Sang Weihan urged the Young Emperor to seek peace with the Khitan to ease the state's peril; the Young Emperor agreed and sent envoys submitting a memorial styling himself subject, with humble words acknowledging fault first.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan raided year after year; the Jin court was worn out and the border people knew no peace. Chancellor Sang Weihan urged the Young Emperor to sue for peace. He agreed and sent envoys with a humble memorial acknowledging fault and styling himself a subject.

sentences.zh: 使回，德光報曰：「但使桑維翰、景延廣自來，並割鎮、定與我，則可通和也。

translations.literal: When the envoys returned, Deguang replied: "Only if Sang Weihan and Jing Yanguang come themselves, and moreover cede Zhen and Ding to me, then peace can be opened."
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys returned, Deguang replied, "Peace is possible only if Sang Weihan and Jing Yanguang come in person and you cede Zhen and Ding to me."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷知其不可，乃止。

translations.literal: " The court knew this was impossible and therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The court knew this was impossible and abandoned the effort.

sentences.zh: 時契丹諸部頻年出征，蕃國君臣稍厭兵革，德光母嘗謂蕃漢臣僚曰：「南朝漢兒爭得一向臥耶！

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan tribes for successive years went on campaign; the barbarian state's ruler and ministers gradually grew weary of arms. Deguang's mother once said to barbarian and Han officials: "How can the Han fellows of the southern dynasty keep lying down all the time!"
translations.idiomatic: After years of campaigning, Khitan rulers and ministers were growing weary of war. Deguang's mother once told her officials, "Must those southern Han always keep us awake?"

sentences.zh: 自古及今，惟聞漢來和蕃，不聞蕃去和漢，待伊漢兒的當回心，則我亦不惜通好也。」

translations.literal: From antiquity to the present one has only heard of Han coming to make peace with barbarians, not heard of barbarians going to make peace with Han. Wait until those Han fellows come around, then I too will not be sparing of opening friendly relations."
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity until now one has only heard of Han suing barbarians for peace, never the reverse. When those Han come to their senses, I too will not refuse peace."

sentences.zh: 三年，樂壽監軍王巒繼有密奏，苦言瀛、鄚可取之狀。

translations.literal: In the third year the military supervisor of Leshou Wang Luan repeatedly sent secret memorials bitterly describing how Ying and Mo could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Wang Luan, military supervisor of Leshou, sent repeated secret memorials insisting that Ying and Mo could be seized.

sentences.zh: 十月，少帝遣杜重威、李守貞等率兵經略。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Young Emperor sent Du Chongwei, Li Shouzhen, and others to lead troops on a strategic campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Young Emperor sent Du Chongwei, Li Shouzhen, and others on campaign.

sentences.zh: 十一月，蕃將高牟翰敗晉師於瀛州之北，梁漢璋死之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the barbarian general Gao Mouhan defeated Jin troops north of Yingzhou; Liang Hanzhang died in it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Khitan general Gao Mouhan routed the Jin army north of Yingzhou; Liang Hanzhang was killed.

sentences.zh: 契丹主聞晉既出師，自率諸部由易、定抵鎮州，杜重威等自瀛州西趨常山，至中渡橋，敵已至矣，兩軍隔滹水而寨焉。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler, hearing the Jin had already sent troops out, personally led the tribes from Yi and Ding to reach Zhenzhou. Du Chongwei and others from Yingzhou hurried west toward Changshan; reaching Middle Crossing Bridge, the enemy had already arrived; the two armies camped facing each other across the Hutuo River.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the Jin had marched, the Khitan ruler led his tribes from Yi and Ding to Zhenzhou. Du Chongwei hurried west from Yingzhou toward Changshan and reached Middle Crossing Bridge, where the enemy already waited; the two armies encamped on opposite banks of the Hutuo River.

sentences.zh: 十二月十日，杜重威率諸軍降於契丹，語在《晉少帝紀》中。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the twelfth month Du Chongwei led the various armies to surrender to the Khitan; the account is in the "Annals of the Young Emperor of Jin."
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day of the twelfth month Du Chongwei surrendered his entire army to the Khitan; the fuller account appears in the Annals of the Young Emperor of Jin.

sentences.zh: 十二日，德光入鎮州，大犒將士。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day Deguang entered Zhenzhou and lavishly rewarded officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day Deguang entered Zhenzhou and lavished rewards on his troops.

sentences.zh: 十四日，自鎮州南行，中渡降軍所釋甲仗百萬計，並令於鎮州收貯，戰馬數萬匹，長驅而北。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day he went south from Zhenzhou. The surrendered troops at Middle Crossing had cast off armor and weapons numbering on the order of a million; he ordered them all stored at Zhenzhou, war horses numbering tens of thousands, and drove straight north.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth he marched south from Zhenzhou. The surrendered Jin army had abandoned arms in the millions, which he ordered stored at Zhenzhou, along with tens of thousands of horses, before driving north.

sentences.zh: 命張彥澤領二千騎先趨東京，遣重威部轄降兵取邢、相路前進。

translations.literal: He ordered Zhang Yanze to lead two thousand horsemen to hurry first to the Eastern Capital, and sent Chongwei to command the surrendered troops along the Xing and Xiang route to advance.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Yanze ahead with two thousand horsemen toward the Eastern Capital and ordered Chongwei to lead the surrendered troops along the Xing and Xiang route.

sentences.zh: 晉少帝遣子延煦、延寶奉降表於契丹，並傳國寶一紐至牙帳。

translations.literal: The Young Emperor of Jin sent his sons Yanshu and Yanbao to present the surrender memorial to the Khitan, and also transmitted the string of state treasures to the yak-tail tent.
translations.idiomatic: The Young Emperor sent his sons Yanshu and Yanbao with the surrender memorial and the imperial regalia to the Khitan headquarters.

sentences.zh: 明年春正月朔日，德光至汴北，文武百官迎於路。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of spring the next year, Deguang reached north of Bian; civil and military officials welcomed him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the following spring Deguang reached the north bank of Bian, where civil and military officials lined the road to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 是日入宮，至昏復出，次於赤崗。

translations.literal: That day he entered the palace; at dusk he came out again and halted at Red Mound.
translations.idiomatic: That day he entered the palace but withdrew at dusk and camped at Red Mound.

sentences.zh: 五日，宣制降晉少帝為負義侯，於黃龍府安置。

translations.literal: On the fifth day he proclaimed an edict demoting the Young Emperor of Jin to Marquis Who Betrayed Righteousness, to be settled at Huanglong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day he issued an edict demoting the Young Emperor to Marquis Who Betrayed Righteousness and exiling him to Huanglong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七日，德光復自赤崗入居於大內，分命使臣於京城及往諸道括借錢帛。

translations.literal: On the seventh day Deguang again from Red Mound entered and dwelt in the great inner palace, separately ordering envoys in the capital and to the various circuits to levy and borrow money and silks.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day he re-entered the inner palace from Red Mound and sent agents through the capital and the provinces to levy money and silks by force.

sentences.zh: 偽命以李崧為西廳樞密使，以馮道為太傅，以左僕射和凝及北來翰林學士承旨張礪為宰相。

translations.literal: He falsely appointed Li Song as western-hall commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Feng Dao as Grand Tutor, Left Vice Director He Ning and the northern-arrival Hanlin academician recipient Zhang Li as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Li Song western-hall commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Feng Dao Grand Tutor, and He Ning and the northern scholar Zhang Li as chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 二月朔日，德光服漢法服，坐崇元殿受蕃漢朝賀，宣制大赦天下，改晉國為大遼國。

translations.literal: On the first day of the second month Deguang wore Han court robes, sat in Chongyuan Hall to receive congratulations from barbarians and Han, proclaimed an edict granting a great amnesty to all under Heaven, and changed the state of Jin to the Great Liao state.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the second month Deguang wore Chinese court dress, took his seat in Chongyuan Hall to receive congratulations from Khitan and Han officials, proclaimed a general amnesty, and renamed the Jin state as Great Liao.

sentences.zh: 以趙延壽為大丞相，兼政事令，充樞密使兼中京留守。

translations.literal: He appointed Zhao Yanshou Grand Chancellor, concurrently Director of Affairs, filling the post of commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrently Central Capital military governor.
translations.idiomatic: He made Zhao Yanshou Grand Chancellor and Director of Affairs, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and governor of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 降東京為防禦州，尋復為宣武軍。

translations.literal: He demoted the Eastern Capital to a defense prefecture, and shortly restored it as the Xuanwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He reduced the Eastern Capital to a defense prefecture, then soon restored it as the Xuanwu command.

sentences.zh: 十五日，漢高祖建號於晉陽，德光聞之，削奪漢祖官爵。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day the Han Founding Emperor established his reign title at Jinyang; Deguang heard of it and stripped the Han ancestor of office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day the Han Founding Emperor proclaimed his reign at Jinyang. Hearing this, Deguang stripped him of rank and title.

sentences.zh: 是月，晉州、潞州並歸河東。

translations.literal: That month Jin and Lu prefectures both returned to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: That month Jin and Lu prefectures both returned to Hedong control.

sentences.zh: 時盜賊所在群起，攻劫州郡，斷澶州浮梁。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose in groups everywhere, attacking and plundering prefectures and commanderies, and cutting the floating bridge at Chanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits rose everywhere, raiding prefectures and severing the floating bridge at Chanzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹大恐，沿河諸藩鎮並以腹心鎮之。

translations.literal: The Khitan were greatly afraid; the various military governors along the river all garrisoned them with trusted men.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were terrified and posted trusted commanders along the river route.

sentences.zh: 三月朔日，德光坐崇元殿，行入閣之禮，睹漢家儀法之盛，大悅。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month Deguang sat in Chongyuan Hall and performed the rite of entering the pavilion; seeing the splendor of Han court ritual and law, he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month Deguang sat in Chongyuan Hall for the rite of entering the pavilion, marveled at the grandeur of Han court ceremony, and was delighted.

sentences.zh: 以其大將蕭翰為汴州節度使。

translations.literal: He appointed his great general Xiao Han military governor of Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his general Xiao Han military governor of Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 十七日，德光北還。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day Deguang returned north.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth day Deguang marched back north.

sentences.zh: 發離東京，宿於赤岡，有大聲如雷，起於牙帳之下，契丹自黎陽濟河，次湯陰縣界，有一岡，土人謂之愁死岡，德光憩於其上，謂宣徽使高勛曰：「我在上國，以打圍食肉為樂，自及漢地，每每不快，我若得歸本土，死亦無恨。

translations.literal: Setting out from the Eastern Capital, he lodged at Red Mound; there was a great sound like thunder rising beneath the yak-tail tent. The Khitan crossed the river from Liyang and halted at the border of Tangyin County; there was a mound the locals called Mound of Dying from Grief. Deguang rested upon it and said to the commissioner of the Palace Secretariat Gao Xun: "In my upper state I take pleasure in hunting and eating meat; since reaching Han lands I am constantly displeased. If I can return to my native soil, I will die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the Eastern Capital he camped at Red Mound when a thunderous sound rose beneath his tent. The Khitan crossed the river at Liyang and halted in Tangyin, at a hill locals called the Mound of Dying from Grief. Resting there, Deguang told Palace Secretariat Commissioner Gao Xun, "At home I took joy in the hunt and feasting; since entering Han territory I have been miserable. If I can return to my homeland, I will die content."

sentences.zh: 」勛退而謂人曰：「其語偷，殆將死矣。

translations.literal: " Xun withdrew and said to others: "His words are furtive—he is probably about to die."
translations.idiomatic: " Xun withdrew and told others, "His words are those of a dying man."

sentences.zh: 」時賊帥梁暉據相州，德光親率諸部以攻之。

translations.literal: " At that time the bandit chief Liang Hui held Xiangzhou; Deguang personally led the tribes to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: " The bandit Liang Hui then held Xiangzhou, and Deguang personally led his tribes to attack him.

sentences.zh: 四月四日，屠其城而去。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the fourth month he slaughtered the city and departed.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the fourth month he massacred the city and marched on.

sentences.zh: 德光聞河陽軍亂，謂蕃漢臣僚曰：「我有三失：殺上國兵士，打草谷，一失也；

translations.literal: Deguang, hearing of turmoil in the Heyang army, said to barbarian and Han officials: "I have three errors: killing the upper state's soldiers and plundering forage—one error;
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of unrest in the Heyang army, Deguang told his Khitan and Han officials, "I committed three errors: killing soldiers of the upper state and plundering the countryside—that was the first;

sentences.zh: 天下括錢，二失也；

translations.literal: levying money throughout the realm—two errors;
translations.idiomatic: levying money throughout the realm—that was the second;

sentences.zh: 不尋遣節度使歸藩，三失也。

translations.literal: not promptly sending military governors back to their circuits—three errors."
translations.idiomatic: and not promptly sending the military governors back to their posts—that was the third."

sentences.zh: 」十六日，次於欒城縣殺虎林之側，時德光已得寒熱疾數日矣，命部人賫酒脯，禱於得疾之地。

translations.literal: " On the sixteenth day he halted beside Kill-Tiger Grove in Luancheng County. At that time Deguang had already had chills and fever for several days; he ordered tribesmen to carry wine and dried meat and pray at the place where he had fallen ill.
translations.idiomatic: " On the sixteenth day he halted beside Kill-Tiger Grove in Luancheng County. He had been feverish for days and ordered tribesmen to bring wine and dried meat to pray at the place where he had fallen ill.

sentences.zh: 十八日晡時，有大星落於穹廬之前，若迸火而散，德光見之，西望而唾，連呼曰：「劉知遠滅，劉知遠滅！

translations.literal: At the twilight hour of the eighteenth day a great star fell before the domed tent, as if bursting fire and scattering. Deguang saw it, looked west and spat, and repeatedly cried: "Liu Zhiyuan is destroyed! Liu Zhiyuan is destroyed!"
translations.idiomatic: At dusk on the eighteenth a great star fell before his tent like bursting fire. Deguang looked west, spat, and cried again and again, "Liu Zhiyuan is finished! Liu Zhiyuan is finished!"

sentences.zh: 」是月二十一日卒，時年四十六，主契丹凡二十二年。

translations.literal: " On the twenty-first day of that month he died, aged forty-six; he ruled the Khitan for twenty-two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: " He died on the twenty-first day of that month at the age of forty-six, having ruled the Khitan for twenty-two years.

sentences.zh: 契丹人破其屍，摘去腸胃，以鹽沃之，載而北去，漢人目之為「帝羓」焉。

translations.literal: The Khitan broke open his corpse, removed the intestines and stomach, poured salt over it, and carried it north; Han people called it the "emperor's cured meat."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan opened his body, removed the entrails, salted the flesh, and carried it north—the Han called this the "emperor's cured meat."

sentences.zh: （案「以下原本闕佚。

translations.literal: (According to the note: "Below, the original text is missing."
translations.idiomatic: (Note: The original text below is missing.

sentences.zh: 據《五代會要》云：四月十八日，德光卒於欒城。

translations.literal: According to the "Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties," it says: On the eighteenth day of the fourth month, Deguang died at Luancheng.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties, Deguang died at Luancheng on the eighteenth day of the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 五月，宣遣制，以永康王襲位。

translations.literal: In the fifth month an edict was proclaimed appointing Prince Yongkang to succeed to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month an edict proclaimed Prince Yongkang as successor.

sentences.zh: 永康王者，東丹王之長子，以其月二十一日領部族歸國，改會同十年為天祿元年，自稱天授皇帝。

translations.literal: Prince Yongkang was the eldest son of the King of Eastern Dan; on the twenty-first day of that month he led the tribes back to the state, changed the tenth year of Huitong to the first year of Tianlu, and styled himself Emperor Heaven-Granted.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yongkang was the eldest son of the Eastern Dan king. On the twenty-first day of that month he led the tribes home, renamed the tenth Huitong year as Tianlu year 1, and styled himself Emperor Heaven-Granted.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐三年十一月，率騎數萬，陷邢州之內丘縣、深州之饒陽縣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Qianyou of Han, he led several tens of thousands of horsemen and took Neiqiu County of Xingzhou and Raoyang County of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Han Qianyou year 3 he led tens of thousands of horsemen and seized Neiqiu in Xingzhou and Raoyang in Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 周廣順元年正月，太祖命左千牛衛將軍朱憲往修和好，永康王亦遣使報命，獻良馬四匹，太祖復遣尚書左丞田敏、供奉官蔣光遂銜命往聘。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Guangshun of Zhou, the Founding Ancestor ordered the Left General of the Thousand-Ox Guard Zhu Xian to go restore friendly relations; Prince Yongkang also sent envoys in reply, presenting four fine horses. The Founding Ancestor again sent Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Tian Min and the palace attendant Jiang Guangsu bearing credentials on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhou Guangshun year 1 the Zhou founder sent Zhu Xian of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard to restore relations. Yongkang replied with envoys and four fine horses, and the Zhou founder sent Tian Min and Jiang Guangsu on a return mission.

sentences.zh: 其年四月，田敏等回，永康王遣使獻碧玉金鍍銀裹鞍轡，並馬四十匹。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year Tian Min and others returned; Prince Yongkang sent envoys presenting a saddle and bridle of jade-green stone with gold plating and silver wrapping, together with forty horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Tian Min returned, and Yongkang sent gifts of a jade-inlaid saddle with gold and silver fittings and forty horses.

sentences.zh: 其月，太祖又命左金吾將軍姚漢英、左神武將軍華光裔往使。

translations.literal: That month the Founding Ancestor again ordered the Left General of the Golden Crow Guard Yao Hanying and the Left General of the Divine Martial Guard Hua Guangyi to go as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: That same month the Zhou founder sent Yao Hanying and Hua Guangyi on another mission.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，永康王為部下太寧王所弒，德光之子勒所部兵誅太寧王自立，稱應歷元年，號天順皇帝。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year Prince Yongkang was assassinated by his subordinate Prince Taining; Deguang's son Le led the troops under him to execute Prince Taining and establish himself, styling the first year of Yingli and calling himself Emperor Heaven-Compliant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Yongkang was assassinated by his subordinate Prince Taining. Deguang's son Le killed Taining and seized the throne, proclaiming the Yingli era and styling himself Emperor Heaven-Compliant.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年春，太原劉崇將圖南寇，契丹將楊兗率騎萬餘以助之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xiande, Liu Chong of Taiyuan was about to plan a southern raid; the Khitan general Yang Yan led more than ten thousand horsemen to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Xiande year 1 Liu Chong of Taiyuan prepared a southern invasion, and the Khitan general Yang Yan led more than ten thousand horsemen to assist him.

sentences.zh: 三月，世宗親征，與崇戰於潞州高平縣之南原，崇軍大敗，契丹眾棄甲而遁。

translations.literal: In the third month Emperor Shizong personally campaigned and fought Chong on the southern plain of Gaoping County in Luzhou; Chong's army was greatly defeated, and the Khitan masses cast off armor and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Emperor Shizong campaigned in person and met Liu Chong on the southern plain of Gaoping in Luzhou. Chong's army was routed and the Khitan horsemen threw off their armor and fled.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，命許州節度使王彥超等築壘於李晏口，與契丹數千騎戰於安平縣，敗之。）〉

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year he ordered the military governor of Xuzhou Wang Yanchao and others to build fortifications at Li Yankou; they fought several thousand Khitan horsemen at Anping County and defeated them.) )
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 2 he ordered Wang Yanchao of Xuzhou and others to build fortifications at Li Yankou, fought several thousand Khitan horsemen at Anping County, and defeated them.) )
